title: Generalized nonsymmetric cartesian algebras reconstructed from product cones
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $p:\mathcal M\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be a small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad as defined in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], with Kan zero fibre and incidence axiom including both vertex and edge projections. Let $B$ be any infinity category with finite products. Let $B^\times\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be the pullback of the cartesian symmetric monoidal category of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope] along the ordered-block functor $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Fin}_*$. This functor takes $[r]$ to $\langle r\rangle$ and sends input $i$ to output $j$ if $a(j-1)<i\leq a(j)$ for the opposite ordinal map $a:[s]\to[r]$, and to the basepoint otherwise.

There is a coherent total-product functor $\Pi:B^\times\to B$. On a tuple it takes the finite product, and on an arrow its output components are the block maps precomposed with projections from the full input product; the degree-zero product is terminal. Let $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal M}(B)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M,B)$ on functors $M$ for which the inert projections exhibit
$$M(m)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^r M(m_i)\quad(m\in\mathcal M_{[r]}),$$
including a terminal value on every object over $[0]$. Then composition with $\Pi$ induces an equivalence from the full category of inert-preserving functors $\mathcal M\to B^\times$ over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ to $\operatorname{Mon}_{\mathcal M}(B)$. At $m$ an inverse has tuple $(M(m_1),\ldots,M(m_r))$. On an arrow $m\to m'$ its $j$th block map is obtained by first projecting $m$ to that consecutive block, then applying the induced arrow to $m'_j$, and using the product-cone equivalence for that block. The inverse is a coherent functor, including all transformations and higher simplices, and the space of inverse lifts with the specified product-cone identification is contractible. These assertions are natural under inert-preserving operad maps and finite-product-preserving functors in $B$. No terminality of $\mathcal M_{[0]}$, and no colimits in $B$ or cocartesian lifts of active arrows in $\mathcal M$, are assumed.
